_comment: WATCHDOG session permissions. Watchdog server only -- no motion/gripper/scene rule, so a config mistake that leaked a command server into this session would still prompt before the arm could be moved. The deny list is the session-level half of the independence guarantee: role_context.py notes that role is derived from the environment and get_rendered_task is hosted only on this role's server, so 'neither role has any tool capable of naming the other's file'. That holds at the MCP layer only. A watchdog session with Read can open agents/tasks/fmb_assembly.executor.yaml directly, and one that can spawn a subagent can have it do the reading under its own permissions -- either way the watchdog learns the executor's rendering, which is the one thing the two-file split exists to prevent. The watchdog observes through its MCP tools (get_execution_state, get_events, get_evidence, wait_for_event) and records through record_verdict, all server-side; it needs no filesystem, shell, or network access to do its job. Workflow is denied for the same reason Agent and Task are: it orchestrates subagents, which read under their own permissions. Artifact and ShareOnboardingGuide are denied as OUTBOUND channels rather than read vectors -- neither can open the executor's file, but both can publish this session's content off the machine, and a scored run's transcript should not leave it. Skill is denied because a skill injects instructions into the session, which is not something a scored watchdog's reasoning should be open to.
_run_params_comment: RUN PARAMETERS -- edit these two before a run; they are the only knobs here that change behaviour rather than permissions. model: an alias ('opus', 'sonnet', 'haiku', 'fable') or a full id ('claude-sonnet-5'). effortLevel: one of low, medium, high, xhigh, max. Both are read by Claude Code from this file because run_watchdog.sh passes it with --settings, and a --settings file outranks ~/.claude/settings.json -- which is the point: without the model key here a scored run silently inherits whatever model the operator last set globally, and the run record could not say which model produced it. The launcher echoes both values at startup; record them with the run (see RUN.md step 3). Deleting effortLevel restores the model's own default ('auto'); there is no literal 'auto' value to write. Currently BOTH roles run claude-sonnet-5 at low effort, deliberately matched so the two sides of a run differ only in role. If you ever want them to differ, the reason to raise this one first is that WatchDog's turns are conformance judgment -- arming discipline, trigger-versus-bound adjudication -- while the executor's are mechanical skill calls; that is the same split recorded for the API path in agents/config/*.yaml. A --effort or --model flag on the command line, and the CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL / ANTHROPIC_MODEL env vars, all outrank this file, so leave them unset for a scored run.

permissions._deny_comment: Verified empirically against Claude Code 2.1.280 on 2026-09-22: with these settings a watchdog session asked to read agents/tasks/fmb_assembly_2.executor.yaml reports it has no file-read or shell tool, and a deferred-tool search for one returns nothing. Re-verify after a CLI upgrade -- the tool surface changed between 2.1.88 (which RUN.md was written against) and 2.1.280, and a tool added later is permitted by default. The entries below that name tools not present in a given version are harmless.
